subject: "Fitted" values for unmarked Occu - Does it estimate occupancy based on detection history?

messages.author: 326458640264b495
messages.subject: "Fitted" values for unmarked Occu - Does it estimate occupancy based on detection history?
parts:
Hello all,

The short version: what exactly is the "matrix of expected values" returned by "fitted" from an unmarkedOccuFrame?

Shockingly naive question, but I've been unable to find a satisfactory answer in the package guide or elsewhere on this forum, any help appreciated!

The longer version:

I have camera trap data with both site and observation level covariates for detection, and site covariates for occupancy (although not all are included in all models, I performed model ranking to determine relevant covariates).

I would like a single value, for each camera site, estimating a probability of occupancy based on it's covariates and the detection history at that site, and detection probabilities from other site's histories to account for imperfect detection. Is this what the code "fitted(fm)" will delivery? My output varies by each day, I'm imagining as a result of the daily detection covariate, but are these values actually occupancy? I have seen mention elsewhere of aggregating across fitted values (for bootstrapping, etc) and am curious if that is the approach to take here?

I was not using the Predict function because I am not trying to estimate what occupancy would be under certain set circumstances, rather for each site with the observed data.

If there is an obvious line in the documentation I am missing my apologies, or if you can direct me to read something elsewhere I would value it very much!

Thanks,
Bryn

messages.author: 4a15de51da4445ae
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] "Fitted" values for unmarked Occu - Does it estimate occupancy based on detection history?
parts:
hi Bryn,

 The fitted values are E(y_{ij}) = p_{ij}*psi_{I}  (i.e., the combined product of detection and occupancy)

 From your description I think what you want is an estimate of E(z_{I} | data at site i) which can be obtained from the ranef function (see p. 569 in the Kery and Royle AHM book).

 There is considerable guidance on goodness-of-fit in these models starting on page 589 of the AHM book...

regards,
andy

Hello all,

I'm a new user of unmarked package, and I'm facing a few problems. 
I really hope someone can help me. 

My main problem is very similar to Bryn's questioning, but in my case, involves "pcount".
I have a set of 18 sites (lakes) and 8 sample occasions (months). 
Some sites I sampled once, and the rest I could sampled two to four times each (Total = 44 visits). 


My best model indicated effects of two sites covariates on the abundance, and on detection I did not include covars. 

Even after running a Gof test (chat = 2.95) and subsequent procedures (ranking by QAICc), I couldn't undestrand or find the estimates of abundance for each site.

What am I doing wrong?

Help me, please.


Best wishes, 
Mari

messages.author: 00ebeb6e0521112d
messages.subject: RE: [unmarked] Re: "Fitted" values for unmarked Occu - Does it estimate occupancy based on detection history?
parts:
Dear Mari, and hello Bryn,

your observed data is a site-by-visit matrix of counts (or of detection/nondetection data in the case of Bryn). The fitted values are the expected data under the model, i.e., doing 'fitted(name of fitted model object)' returns a matrix of the same dimensions as your input data, which contain the values of lambda_hat * p_hat, i.e., the expected count at site i and during visit j, based on the parameters for lambda and p estimated by the model from your data.

But this is not what either of you want. To characterize the relationships between a covariate (or more than one covariate) and either abundance (or occupancy) or detection, you need to use the predict function. Setting the argument 'type' to either the state (= occupancy or abundance) or detection and providing a data set with the values of the covariates at which you want to predict will provide you with what you want.

This is actually shown in the unmarked overview vignette, here: https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/unmarked/vignettes/unmarked.pdf

Best regards  --- Marc
